questions.title: What does Rule 404(b) consider intrinsic evidence in a felon‑in‑possession case?
questions.question_body: In the opinion the district court allowed D.F. to testify that she had seen Cutbank with the sawed‑off Marlin before the incident, citing United States v. Battle. I’m confused about what makes this testimony “intrinsic” versus “extrinsic.” Does any prior possession of a firearm automatically satisfy Rule 404(b) in a felon‑in‑possession or is there a higher threshold? What distinguishing factors determine whether such prior‑possession evidence is admissible?

questions.title: How does the Confrontation Clause treat a witness’s prior statements to police when that witness also testifies?
questions.question_body: The court says the Confrontation Clause is satisfied because D.F. “actually appear[s] in court and testify[s] in person.” How does that rule apply when the statements she made to police were made before she took the stand? Does the fact that she later testifies remove the hearsay exception? In what scenario would such prior statements still be considered inadmissible under the Confrontation Clause?

questions.title: What is the harmless‑error standard for evidentiary rulings, and how was it applied here?
questions.question_body: The opinion frequently references the doctrine that trials can be upheld if the error was harmless and cites cases like DeMarce and Keys. I’m not sure how the court determines whether an evidentiary error is harmless. What is the standard for assessing prejudice, the cumulative effect of errors, and how does it guide appellate reversal in this context?

questions.title: How is the 4‑level USSG § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) firearms enhancement calculated?
questions.question_body: The district court applied a 4‑level increase because the firearm was used in connection with another felony. The opinion states this applies regardless of whether a criminal charge was brought or a conviction obtained. What exact facts must the district court find to justify this enhancement, and how does the presence of an altered or obliterated serial number factor into that calculation?

questions.title: Does an altered or obliterated serial number automatically trigger a 4‑level enhancement?
questions.question_body: The opinion mentions a 2‑level increase for an altered serial number. Does that always apply, or is there more nuance? Under what circumstances would a court discount the serial‑number alteration when applying § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B), and how is that distinguished from the 4‑level enhancement?

questions.title: Why must the appellate court confirm that the district court considered § 3553(a) factors when reviewing a sentence?
questions.question_body: The appellate court discusses that the district court must have "actually considered" the 3553(a) factors, but it does not need to provide a mechanical recitation. What are the specific 3553(a) factors that a district court typically weighs, and how does the absence of an explicit recitation affect the appellate court’s ability to find a sentence unreasonable?

questions.title: How does the Presentence Investigation Report (PSR) interact with sentencing memoranda in appellate review of guideline ranges?
questions.question_body: The opinion notes that the PSR provided factual statements that the court adopted without objection. What is the role of the PSR in determining the advisory guidelines range, and how does appellate review treat errors that may arise from inaccuracies in the PSR versus errors in the district court’s own analysis?
